newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, prices to hold ground.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, prices to hold ground.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in modest trade on Friday and traders predicted prices would hold ground despite modest trade caused by lack of foreign buyers.
"When (blue chips) Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka do not trade much, it always points to smaller turnover," Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage told Reuters.
He said foreign investors were turned off by complicated red tape which slows down ownership registration.
Drugs firm Pliva edged up seven kuna to 480, selling 180 units, while fully listed Zagrebacka Banka gained nine kuna, with only four shares changing hands.
Friday's turnover was lower at 2.9 million kuna and volume halved at 7,327 shares.
Of 12 active stocks, six rose, four fell and two were unchanged.
Confectioner Kras, rising 28 kuna to 525, led the gainers selling 1,597 shares.
"Kras has very good characteristics so nothing prevents it from being a stable stock. There are some indications it will rise further," said Zelimorski.
Last Thursday Kras announced it was about to close an investment agreement with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Food company Podravka was the most actively traded stock. It edged down two kuna to close at 317 kuna with 2,236 units sold.
"This is a wonderful share which confirmed its solidity by selling loss-making companies not long ago," Zelimorski said, adding that its price would at least hold its ground.
Hoteliers Istraturist and Jadranturist had negligible losses, selling 1,179 and 537 shares respectively. Laguna stood out, gaining 40 kuna to 1,440 with 153 shares changing hands.
Riviera edged up two kuna to 182 on volume of 342 and Suncani Hvar ended flat at 67 kuna.
The leading decliner was cable maker Elka, which lost five kuna to 170 trading 478 units.
